saints.name: Sts. Protus and Hyacinth
saints.title: Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: Two early Roman martyrs, remembered as brothers, whose tombs on the Old Salarian Way were honoured from the earliest centuries…
biography: Protus and Hyacinth were martyrs of the Roman Church, venerated from the earliest times and traditionally held to be brothers who suffered under the persecutions of the third century. They were buried in the cemetery of Basilla on the Old Salarian Way, where their graves were marked and adorned by later popes.

The historical reality of their cult was strikingly confirmed in 1845, when the untouched tomb of Hyacinth was found in the catacomb, its original inscription still in place and the martyr's ashes within. Their names have been kept in the Roman calendar and canon of the Mass from ancient days.
saints.knownFor: Their witness of blood in early Roman persecution.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain), 11 September
